app.title: Browser automation
app.subtitle: AUTOMATION PORTAL

scenes.new_notice: Creating a scenario makes a v1 draft with a single step that opens a page. Change it into the real steps on the edit page.
scenes.new_id: Scenario ID (lowercase letters, digits, - or _; it cannot be changed or reused)
revision.id_mismatch: The id in the scenario file must be {id} (scenario IDs cannot change)
revision.extra_file: {path} is not used by this scenario
revision.no_scenario: The scenario file scenario.yaml is missing
scene.not_published: Nothing is published yet: validate a revision, publish it once it passes, then run it.
scene.newer_draft: Runs use the published v{published}; v{latest} is used only after it passes validation and is published.
scene.versions_hint: Revisions are immutable; editing creates a new revision
scene.base_url_hint: Prefilled when validating and running. Leave empty to use the baseUrl in the scenario file ({default}).
spec.name: Name
edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.older: This is the older v{shown}. Saving creates a new revision with this content (the latest is v{latest}).
edit.notice: The files are validated before saving; nothing is saved if there are problems. A new revision must pass validation before it can be published.
edit.note_placeholder: For example: use the new submit button
run_form.description_validation: Runs v{number} in a real browser; once it passes, this revision can be published.
run_form.notice_validation: Validation really operates the target site, including steps with side effects such as creating records. Use a test environment or test data.
run_form.notice_execution: Operates the target site with the published revision. Steps with side effects are never retried automatically.
run_form.inputs_hint: Defaults are filled in; inputs without a default must be filled in. Values can be dynamic, e.g. {{{{today}}}}, {{{{today+1}}}} or {{{{random:10:30}}}}, and are replaced with the current value when the run starts. They are checked first, and the browser is not started if any input is invalid.
run_form.window_hint: Headed mode opens a browser window on the computer that runs the job (this one or a remote worker), so you can watch every step; headless mode runs in the background without disturbing whoever is using that computer.
run_form.window_unavailable: The computer that would run this has no graphical desktop (for example a Linux server without DISPLAY), so only headless mode is available.
run_form.base_url_hint: Overrides the baseUrl in the scenario file. Leave empty to use the scenario file.
runs.description: Filter by category, scenario and result. Every run keeps its inputs, outputs, steps, assertions and screenshots.
run.title: Run {id}
run.replay_before_publish: Before publishing, you can watch the recording of this validation.
run.polling: Running; this page updates when the status changes.
run.newer_validation: The latest validation of this revision did not pass, so this result cannot be used to publish it. Validate it again.
run.interrupted: The server restarted and interrupted this run; run it again
run.hash_mismatch: The content that ran does not match the revision hash, so this validation does not count
run.scenario_invalid: The scenario file has {count} problem(s) and cannot run
run.crashed: The run failed with an error: {detail}
run.worker_outdated: The app on Worker “{name}” is too old to understand {features} used by this scenario (for example the iframe or new-tab syntax). Update RPA Worker and run again
error.revision_unreadable: The files of scenario {id} v{number} are missing or no longer valid

error.revision_invalid: {count} problem(s) found; no revision was created
error.scene_exists: The scenario ID {id} is already used (including archived scenarios); choose another
error.revision_conflict: Someone just saved a new revision of {id}; reload and edit again

error.no_examples: The examples folder was not found (RPA_EXAMPLES_DIR)
error.inputs_invalid: {count} input problem(s); the run was not started
error.not_validated: Scenario {id} v{number} has not passed validation and cannot be published
error.content_changed: The files of scenario {id} v{number} differ from what was validated; it cannot be published
error.file_not_found: {path} is not in the run folder
error.base_url_invalid: The URL must start with http or https: {value}
error_page.title: Something went wrong
server.sqlite_notice: Using SQLite: for development and prototypes only. Set RPA_DATABASE_URL to PostgreSQL in production
server.recovered: {count} run(s) were interrupted when the server stopped and are marked as failed
server.pack_problems: The folder of domain {domain} has {count} error(s); items with problems were not loaded. See the domain page for details
template.comment: New scenario: change browser.baseUrl and steps into the real actions, save a new revision, then validate it. See docs/design/dsl.html
js.save_failed: That did not work; try again
js.publish_body: After publishing, runs use this revision; earlier published revisions stay in the history. Publish it?
js.cancel_body: The browser stops right away. Actions already completed on the target site are not undone.
js.stale_base: Someone saved a newer revision; reload and edit again
js.json_invalid: The inputs must be a JSON object (names and values inside curly braces)
domain.testsite_description: Real cases that run against the local test site (started by rpa serve at http://127.0.0.1:8765): create a record, look it up, look up a record that does not exist, the Python script version of creating a record, and examples for two login roles.
domain.empty: No scenarios in this domain yet. Create one, or move a scenario here from its Run settings.
domain.unassigned_description: Scenarios and roles not yet assigned to a domain. Created automatically when upgrading to domain folders; move them in a scenario's run settings or by editing a role.
domain.reload_title: Read this domain's folder again (after editing files outside the Portal)
domain.problems: The domain folder has {count} problem(s); items with problems were not loaded
domain.composites_description: A domain holding only composite scenarios, which may use scenarios from other domains. Created automatically when upgrading to domain folders; existing composite scenarios are placed here.
domain.sync_title: This domain's git source, sync state, pull and push
card.tag_title: Category; the scenario type when there is none
card.debug_title: Validate the latest v{number}: it really operates the target site and can be published once it passes
domains.description: Group scenarios by target system or business area, for example Google automation or Microsoft automation. Each domain is an item in the Scenarios side menu.
domains.unassigned_hint: Choose a domain in the scenario's Run settings
domains.new_notice: For example: ID google, name “Google automation”. The ID is used in addresses and cannot be changed later.
domains.server_hint: The name goes into revision, validation and publication records, and is the default committer when pushing
domains.git_ready: Available (only this server pulls and pushes)
domains.git_notice: Enter the repository URL and directory, then Test connection: if the directory has a pack.yaml, its ID and name are filled in and pulled; if the directory does not exist yet, an empty domain is created and the first push creates the directory.
domains.git_ssh_hint: SSH repositories: create the domain with Add domain first, then generate a deploy key on its Sync page.
domains.order_hint: Use ↑ ↓ to change the order; the domain menus under Scenarios follow it
domains.composites_hint: Not listed under Scenarios; composite scenarios are managed in the projects under Projects
projects.description: Projects are the items in the Projects menu. Each project is its own composite automation board with its own set of composite scenarios.
projects.empty: No projects yet. Press “New project” to create the first one.
projects.order_hint: Use ↑ ↓ to change the order; the Projects menu follows it
projects.unassigned_hint: Open the composite scenario and choose a project under “Code, domain, project and archive”
projects.new_notice: For example: ID billing, name “Billing project”. The ID is used in addresses and cannot be changed later. Projects exist only on this server and are not written to domain folders or git.
project.empty: This project has no composite scenarios yet. Press “New composite scenario”, or move one here under “Code, domain, project and archive” on its page.
project.composites_description: Created automatically on upgrade; holds the composite scenarios you already had.
error.domain_id_invalid: Invalid domain ID "{id}": start with a lowercase letter or digit and use only lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (at most 64)
error.domain_exists: The domain ID {id} is already used; choose another
error.domain_not_empty: Domain {id} still has {count} scenario(s), including archived ones; move them to another domain first
error.domain_order_changed: The list of domains has changed (a domain was added or deleted elsewhere). Reload the page and change the order again
error.project_id_invalid: Invalid project ID "{id}": start with a lowercase letter or digit and use only lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (at most 64)
error.project_exists: The project ID {id} is already used; choose another
error.project_not_empty: Project {id} still has {count} composite scenario(s), including archived ones; delete them or move them to another project first
error.project_order_changed: The list of projects has changed (a project was added or deleted elsewhere). Reload the page and change the order again
error.display_unavailable: The computer that would run this has no graphical desktop, so it cannot show a browser window; use headless mode or choose another place to run.
js.domain_delete_body: The domain will disappear from the side menu. Delete it?
js.project_delete_body: The project will disappear from the Projects menu. Delete it?
card.step_debug_title: Step debugging: run one step at a time and see the screenshot, URL and page facts; validate from the debugging page
scene.verifications_hint: One per validation, synced with the domain folder; a passed record with a matching hash allows publishing, whichever server ran it
roles.description: Register how each test account logs in and how to tell it is logged in; scenarios use it with login: {{ role: … }}. Each role keeps its own login state, never shared.
roles.notice: Before a run, the role's login is checked; if it is not logged in the run stops at "Login required" without running any step. "Log in" opens a browser window on the computer running the Portal so you can log in yourself (SSO, captchas and two-factor all work); the login state is stored only in this computer's data folder, readable only by you.
roles.notice_via_recorder: Before a run, the role's login is checked; if it is not logged in the run stops at "Login required" without running any step. Through a recorder, "Log in" opens a browser window on the recorder you are using so you can log in yourself (SSO, captchas and two-factor all work); the login state is sent back and stored in the server's data folder.
roles.no_display: The computer running the Portal has no display, so manual login is not available here: open the management Portal through the RPA Recorder and log in there (the browser opens on the recorder's computer), or give the role automatic login steps.
roles.no_display_via_recorder: This recorder has no display, so a browser window for manual login cannot be opened; you can give the role automatic login steps instead.
roles.empty: No login roles yet. Add a role here when a scenario needs to log in.
roles.session_waiting: A browser window is open on the computer running the Portal: log in there, then press "Finish login" or simply close the window.
roles.session_waiting_via_recorder: A browser window is open on this recorder: log in there, then press "Finish login" or simply close the window.
roles.login_title: Open a browser window on the Portal's computer and log in yourself
roles.login_title_via_recorder: Open a browser window on this recorder and log in yourself
roles.check_title: Check in a headless browser whether the login is still valid (logs in automatically when automatic login steps exist)
roles.check_unavailable: The server has not downloaded {browser}: open the Portal through the RPA Recorder to check on the recorder. Runs also check first on the computer running them.
roles.form_notice: For example: id erp-clerk, name "ERP clerk". The id goes into a scenario's login.role and cannot be changed later.
roles.form_description: Description (optional, e.g. which test account; never a password)
roles.form_check_url_placeholder: A page only visible when logged in; empty means the login URL
roles.form_check: Element visible only when logged in (DSL locator)
roles.form_check_hint: e.g. {{ testId: current-user }}, {{ role: button, name: Log out }}, {{ text: My account }}.
roles.form_auto: Automatic login steps (optional, a list of DSL steps)
roles.form_auto_hint: Only for plain username/password systems; use {{{{ secrets.NAME }}}} for the password and set its value under Secrets below. Leave empty for manual login only.
roles.form_domain_hint: The role definition is saved in this domain folder's roles/ and syncs with the domain; the login state stays on this server
secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.hint: Values stay on this computer and are never shown by pages or the API
secrets.hint_via_recorder: Values stay on the server and are never shown by pages or the API
secrets.empty: No secrets yet, and no scenario or role uses one.
secrets.form_notice: The value is stored in secrets.json in the data folder, readable only by you; it is never shown again.
needs.title: Before running
recording.description: Record on this computer or paste a codegen recording → DSL draft → step debugging → validation → publish by hand. Recordings are never published directly.
recording.active: Recording {scene}: the browser window and Playwright Inspector are open on the computer running the Portal; close the browser window when you are done.
recording.active_via_recorder: Recording {scene}: the browser window and Playwright Inspector are open on this recorder; close the browser window when you are done.
recording.in_progress: Recording: use the browser on the computer running the Portal and close its window when you are done; the draft appears here automatically.
recording.in_progress_via_recorder: Recording: use the browser on this recorder and close its window when you are done; the draft appears here automatically.
recording.record_hint: After "Start recording", a browser and the Playwright Inspector open on the computer running the Portal; work as usual and close the browser window when done. Typed values become inputs and password fields become secrets.
recording.record_hint_via_recorder: After "Start recording", a browser and the Playwright Inspector open on this recorder; work as usual and close the browser window when done. Typed values become inputs and password fields become secrets.
recording.paste_hint: Paste the Python generated by Playwright codegen (for example recorded elsewhere with rpa record) to convert it into a draft.
recording.no_display: The computer running the Portal has no display, so it cannot record here: open the management Portal through the RPA Recorder and record there (the browser opens on the recorder's computer), or use Paste a recording.
recording.no_display_via_recorder: This recorder has no display, so it cannot record here; record on a computer with a desktop or paste a recording.
recording.target_existing: A new revision of a scenario
recording.mode_continue_hint: The browser first runs the steps of the current revision (inputs use their defaults), then recording starts from that screen; the recorded steps, inputs, outputs and assertions are appended and nothing existing changes. The Inspector only shows the new actions.
recording.mode_continue_paste_hint: The pasted recording is converted and appended after the existing steps (the existing steps are not run); nothing existing changes.
recording.mode_replace_hint: Record again from the start URL and replace the whole scenario with the recording (name and category are kept, older revisions stay).
recording.script_no_continue: This is a Python script scenario, so it can only be recorded again.
recording.url_continue: Recording continues from the screen where the existing steps end, so no start URL is needed.
recording.continue_needs: The existing steps run before recording continues, but inputs {names} have no default; set defaults on the scenario page or choose “Record again”
recording.replay_failed: Running the existing steps failed at {step}: {message}. Fix it with step debugging first, or choose “Record again”
recording.url_paste_hint: Optional: used as the first step when the recording opens no URL.
recording.cli_hint: You can also record from the command line:
recording.detail_description: The recording and the {scene} draft converted from it.
recording.done_notice: Saved as draft v{number} of {scene}. Next: debug step by step to make sure every element is found, then validate and publish.
recording.raw_hint: Passwords masked; kept as the source, never published
recording.nothing_recorded: Nothing was recorded (the browser may not have opened).
recording.no_actions: No actions were recorded (only the URL was opened); no revision was created.
recording.interrupted: The server restarted and the recording was interrupted; please record again
role.auto_logged_in: Was not logged in; logged in automatically
role.login_done: Logged in; the login state was updated
role.login_ended: The browser ended unexpectedly (exit code {code}); no login state was saved
role.login_not_confirmed: The login did not succeed and the state was not updated; please try again
role.login_timeout: The login took too long; the browser was closed
role.login_not_yet: Not logged in yet: the check URL ended at {url} without the logged-in element. Finish logging in in the browser window, then press "Finish login" again.
role.login_check_failed: Could not confirm the login yet: {detail}
role.login_closed_not_logged_in: The window was closed before logging in (the check URL ended at {url}); the login state was not updated. Log in again.
role.login_unverified: Could not confirm the login, so the login state was not updated: {detail}
role.login_device_outdated: This recorder is an older version that does not confirm the login itself, and the server has not downloaded {browser} to confirm it, so the login state was not updated. Update the RPA Recorder and log in again.
role.check_device_outdated: This recorder is an older version and cannot check logins; update the RPA Recorder.
debug.title: Debug {name}
debug.description: Run one step at a time in a browser, see the page after each step, test locators, and edit the YAML into a new revision.
debug.start_notice: Debugging really operates the target site. Steps with side effects (click, fill, select, check, press) ask for confirmation before running again; no step is ever repeated automatically.
debug.window_hint: Headed mode opens a browser window on the computer running the Portal; both modes show a screenshot after every step on this page.
debug.window_hint_via_recorder: Headed mode opens a browser window on this recorder; both modes show a screenshot after every step on this page.
debug.starting: Starting the browser… (the first Firefox start can take a dozen seconds)
debug.idle_closed: Closed after being idle too long
debug.session_notice: Debugging v{revision} · {engine} · {window}. Closes automatically after {minutes} idle minutes.
debug.no_screenshot: No screenshot yet: run a step or press "Screenshot".
debug.found: Found {count} element(s) (outlined in red in the screenshot)
debug.yaml_hint: Saving creates a new revision and keeps debugging with it; steps that ran are kept by id
debug.save: Save as a new revision and keep debugging
contract.script_notice: This is a Python script scenario: outputs come from assertion.py, and renaming an input does not change the scripts.
contract.note_placeholder: e.g. raise the quantity limit to 50

run.needs_login_hint: After logging in, press "Run again" to repeat the run with the same inputs.

js.role_delete_body: The role and its login state will be deleted. Are you sure?
js.role_clear_body: The role's login state on this computer is deleted; runs stop at "Login required" until you log in again.
js.role_clear_body_via_recorder: The role's login state stored on the server is deleted; runs stop at "Login required" until you log in again.
js.secret_delete_body: Scenarios and roles that use it will fail for a missing secret (unless an environment variable with the same name exists). Are you sure?
js.recording_started: Recording started: use the browser on the computer running the Portal
js.recording_started_via_recorder: Recording started: use the browser on this recorder
js.debug_close_body: The debugging browser is closed; actions already done on the target site are not undone.
role.secret_missing: Not logged in; automatic login needs secrets that are not set: {names}
role.needs_login_run: Run {id} found it was not logged in
error.recording_script: {id} is a Python script scenario and cannot continue after its steps; choose “Record again”
section.description_steps: The automation steps (the steps section of the scenario file). Showing v{shown}; saving rewrites only this section and creates v{next}.
section.description_verify: Independent assertions (the verify section): after the automation they check the page facts, and outputs are published only if all pass. Showing v{shown}; saving rewrites only this section and creates v{next}.
section.hint_steps: Starts with steps:; the other sections (inputs, outputs, assertions, browser settings) are not affected. See “Scenario DSL” in the docs for actions and fields.
section.hint_verify: Starts with verify:; each check names the page fact in value and uses one of notEmpty, equals, contains or matches. Clearing the section removes all assertions (scenarios with outputs need assertions).
section.no_facts: No step reads page content (extract) yet.
section.insert_hint: Click a name to insert it at the cursor.
error.section_unknown: There is no “{key}” section to edit
error.section_script: Python script scenarios have no steps or verify section; edit automation.py and assertion.py
error.section_key: The text must start with “{key}:” and contain only that section
contract.table_hint_inputs: Required inputs have no default. Defaults can be dynamic: {{{{today}}}}, {{{{today+1}}}}, {{{{now}}}} or {{{{random:10:30}}}} are replaced with the current value on every run. Renaming also renames references in the steps. Saving rewrites only the inputs section and creates a new revision (validate it again).
contract.table_hint_outputs: Pick the value from the page facts the steps read. Saving rewrites only the outputs section and creates a new revision (validate it again).
contract.yaml_hint_inputs: Edit the inputs section of the scenario file directly (starting with inputs:). Renaming here does not rename references in the steps; it is validated before switching back to the table.
contract.yaml_hint_outputs: Edit the outputs section of the scenario file directly (starting with outputs:); it is validated before switching back to the table.
error.revision_unpublished: Revision v{number} of scenario {id} has never been published; the playground only uses published revisions
error.workflow_name_missing: Enter a name for the composite scenario
error.workflow_format: The composite scenario definition has {count} format problem(s)
error.stale_workflow: The composite scenario was changed elsewhere (you started from save {base}, it is now at save {latest}); reload and try again
error.workflow_running: Composite scenario {id} is running; delete it after the run ends
error.workflow_run_active: Composite scenario run {id} has not finished
error.workflow_not_resumable: Composite scenario run {id} has no node to continue from; run it again from the start
error.workflow_invalid: The composite scenario has {count} problem(s) and cannot run yet
workflow.revision_unpublished: Node {node}: {scene} v{revision} has never been published; a composite scenario can only pin published revisions
workflow_run.title: Composite scenario run {id}
workflow_run.rerun_title: Run the same composite scenario (same nodes, revisions and input sources) again from the first node
workflow_run.resume_title: Reuse the outputs of the nodes that passed and continue from the node that stopped; earlier actions are not repeated
workflow_run.polling: Running; the page updates every second.
workflow_run.needs_login_hint: After logging in, press “Continue from {node}”: the nodes that already passed are not repeated.
workflow_run.nodes_hint: Run in topological order; all upstream dependencies must pass first
workflow_run.reused_hint: Reused from the earlier run that passed
workflow_run.node_stopped: Node {node} ({scene}): {status}. The composite scenario stopped here and the later nodes did not run
workflow_run.node_inputs_invalid: The inputs of node {node} do not satisfy their rules, so it did not start: {problems}
workflow_run.cancelled: Cancelled; the later nodes did not run
playground.description: Produce reproducible composite scenarios by moving nodes, connecting dependencies and configuring inputs.
playground.no_published: No scenario has been published yet: validate and publish one on its scenario page before adding it to a composite scenario.
playground.empty: No composite scenarios yet. Press “New composite scenario”, then add published scenarios from the library.
playground.import_notice: Import a file downloaded with “Export JSON” to create a new composite scenario.
playground.import_name_placeholder: Leave empty to use the name in the file
workflow.description: Connect pinned published scenarios in a directed acyclic graph.
workflow.notice: A node runs after all its dependencies pass. Successful upstream outputs become downstream inputs. Nodes run one at a time in topological order; failures stop the run and can be resumed.
workflow.problems_hint: Select an issue to locate its node or field
workflow.library_hint: Drag a scene onto the canvas or click to add it.
workflow.run_notice: Run nodes one at a time in dependency order, using each scenario’s URL and pinned version.
run.back_to_workflow: Back to the composite scenario run
run.workflow_node: This is node {node} of the composite scenario run:
run.needs_login_hint_workflow: After logging in, continue from this node on the composite scenario run page.
wfjs.import_invalid: The content is not a JSON object
wfjs.delete_body: Its run history is kept. Delete it?
wfjs.description: Connect pinned published scenarios in a directed acyclic graph.
wfjs.stale: The composite scenario was changed elsewhere; reload and try again
wfjs.fix_problems: Cannot run: resolve the following issues
wfjs.settings_empty: Select a node to set its revision and inputs.
wfjs.newer_revision: The scenario now publishes v{{number}}; this node is pinned to v{{current}}.
wfjs.no_contract: The inputs and outputs of this revision cannot be read
wfjs.cancel_body: The current node stops at once and the later nodes do not run; actions already completed on the target site are not undone.
wfjs.resumed: Continued from the node that stopped
error.worker_id_invalid: Worker ID "{id}" is not valid: start with a lowercase letter or digit, use only lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, at most 64 characters; "local" is reserved for this computer.
error.worker_exists: Device "{id}" is already registered; to get a new invitation, choose "Invite again".
error.worker_busy: Worker "{id}" is running {run}; delete it after the run ends.
error.worker_unauthorized: The token is wrong (inviting again replaces it), or this device is disabled.
error.worker_protocol: The worker speaks protocol version {worker} but the portal speaks {server}: update both computers to the same version (git pull).
error.recorder_protocol: The recorder speaks protocol version {recorder} but the portal speaks {server}: update both to the same version.
error.run_not_assigned: Run {id} is not assigned to this worker, or it has already ended (for example after losing contact).
error.artifacts_invalid: The uploaded run directory is not valid: {detail}
error.run_without_login: The scenario of run {id} has no login role, so no login state can be sent back.
error.role_state_invalid: The login state is not valid: {detail}
error.result_invalid: The run result is not valid: {detail}
error.target_invalid: "{target}" is not a valid place to run; use local, remote or any.
error.no_remote_worker: No remote worker is registered yet: add one on the "Remote workers" page first.
error.local_worker_off: This computer does not run jobs (rpa serve --no-local-worker); choose a remote worker instead.
run.worker_lost: Worker "{worker}" did not report for over a minute and is considered lost; the run is marked failed. Some actions may already have happened on the target system; check before running again.
run.worker_removed: Worker "{worker}", which this run was assigned to, has been deleted.
target.label: Where to run
target.hint: Headed browser windows appear on the computer that runs the job. On a remote worker, 127.0.0.1 means that worker itself (it starts its own test site too).
workers.description: Register the computers that run scenarios (RPA Worker): paste an invitation to pair, then runs go to them and this computer is no longer taken over by headed browser windows.
workers.notice: Devices connect to this computer's external port. A worker claims jobs and sends the report, screenshots and trace back, so run reports look the same as local ones; a recorder opens the browser for recording, step-by-step debugging and manual logins on that computer. Adding a device creates an invitation (single use, valid for 24 hours); paste it into the app on that computer to pair. Inviting again ends the old pairing immediately. A worker that does not report for over a minute is considered lost: its run is marked failed and is not retried automatically (it may already have had side effects).
workers.api_on: The external port is open at {url} (only the Worker API and pairing; a token or invitation is required).
workers.api_off: The external port is not open, so devices cannot connect and no invitation can be created: stop the portal and start it again with rpa serve --worker-port 8081. The portal pages stay local-only.
workers.local_off: This computer does not run jobs (--no-local-worker); every job goes to remote workers.
workers.empty: No devices yet. Choose "Add device" to create an invitation, then paste it into RPA Worker on that computer.
workers.version_differs: Differs from the portal's code: updating both to the same version is safer.
workers.default_hint: Preselected in the run, validation and playground dialogs; you can change it each time.
workers.form_notice: Adding a device creates an invitation (single use, valid for 24 hours); paste it into the app on that computer to pair.
workers.form_id_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, for example win-01; it cannot be changed later.
workers.command_hint: The server address in the invitation is a guess; if the device cannot connect, enter this computer's LAN IP and the code separately in the app (on the command line, use --server with --invite and the code). See the "Remote workers" guide for details.
js.worker_delete_body: The device will no longer be able to connect, and queued runs assigned to it are marked failed. Run history is kept. Continue?
js.worker_disabled: Disabled: this device will not claim jobs.
composites.description: Manage saved composite scenarios, their nodes and recent runs. Open the playground to edit a canvas.
composites.no_description: Open the preview to edit connections and inputs.
playground.start_hint: Create a composite scenario or open an existing canvas. Saved work is managed in a project under Projects.
playground.form_code_placeholder: e.g. order-flow; leave empty for wf-<number>
playground.form_domain_hint: The composite scenario is saved in this domain folder's composites/ and syncs with the domain; it can use scenarios from any domain
workflow.canvas_hint: Drag nodes. Click an upstream right port, then a downstream left port. Select an edge to configure inputs.
wfjs.auto_ambiguous: {{name}}: multiple matching upstream outputs; choose one
wfjs.unlink_hint: Disconnecting clears its output bindings and rechecks input sources.
wfjs.cycle: Cannot connect a node to itself or create a cycle.
wfjs.pick_target: Selected {{node}}. Click a downstream left port. Esc cancels.
wfjs.canvas_hint: Drag nodes. Click an upstream right port, then a downstream left port. Select an edge to configure inputs.
wfjs.library_hint: Drag a scene into the canvas or click to add it.
js.contract_preview_draft: Read-only preview generated from the current contract draft.
js.contract_sample_source: Actual outputs from the latest successful run of v{{number}} · {{run}}
js.contract_sample_empty: No successful output for v{{number}} yet. Validate this revision to see a sample.
js.contract_sample_draft: These values belong to the saved revision; the current draft has not been validated.
js.contract_saved_next: Saved draft v{{number}}. Validate it next, then publish after it passes.
workflow.parameter_hint: Drag an output port to an input, or select the two ports. Auto match uses direct upstream nodes, then script defaults.
wfjs.pick_output: Select an upstream output or drag a wire
wfjs.no_upstream: No upstream node. Connect nodes on the canvas, or use default/manual values.
wfjs.pick_input: Output {{name}} selected. Select an input port; Esc to cancel.
wfjs.incompatible: Output and input types are incompatible. No binding was changed.
wfjs.pinned_contract: This is the node’s pinned, read-only contract. After editing, validate and publish the scene, then select its new revision on this canvas.
wfjs.parameter_hint: Drag an output port to an input, or select the two ports. Auto match uses direct upstream nodes, then script defaults.
workflow.purpose_validation: Validate the latest revision (the result becomes a validation record)
workflow.purpose_unpublished: No published revision yet: validate first, then publish it under Revisions
js.editor_revision: Editing v{{number}}. Further changes create a new revision.
js.contract_preview_invalid: Preview unavailable. Check the current contract; save to see detailed errors.
workers.invite_notice: This invitation is shown only once. It is valid for 24 hours and can be used once; if it is lost or expires, choose "Invite again". It can be exchanged for this device's token, so do not share it.
workers.invite_app: On the worker computer, open RPA Worker and paste this invitation (it has been copied to the clipboard).
workers.command_cli: On a computer with the development setup, you can also pair and start from the command line in the project folder:
js.worker_invite_again_body: The old pairing and token stop working immediately; that device needs the new invitation to connect again. Continue?
js.sync_key_ready: Deploy key generated: add the public key to the repository's Deploy keys with write access
js.sync_disconnect_body: The domain folder stays and becomes a local domain; this server's token, deploy key and working copy are deleted. The remote is not touched.
js.sync_resolve_branch_body: Push the local content to a new branch rpa/<domain>-<time>; open a PR on GitHub, merge it and pull.
js.sync_resolve_remote_body: Back this domain folder up to backups/ first, then replace it with the latest remote content (unpushed local changes stay only in the backup).
js.composite_validate_body: Run this revision's definition once and record the result; once it passes, this revision can be published.

error.invite_invalid: The invitation code is wrong or has already been used: create a new one on the portal's Devices page.
error.invite_expired: The invitation has expired (it is valid for {hours} hours): create a new one on the Devices page.
error.invite_wrong_app: This invitation is for {app}; paste it into that app.
error.invite_needs_port: Open the external port before inviting devices: stop the portal and start it again with rpa serve --worker-port 8081.
target.local_url_warning: This scenario's URL points to this computer (127.0.0.1, localhost). On a remote worker that means the worker itself, so it will probably not reach the site. To run it remotely, change the URL to this computer's LAN address, or choose "This computer".
run.waiting_worker: Waiting for a worker: no remote worker is online, so this run stays queued. Check that the worker computer is running and connected, or cancel this run.
run.waiting_worker_named: Waiting for worker "{name}": this run is assigned to it (for example, a sequence stays on one worker), but it is offline, so the run stays queued. Start that worker or cancel this run.
app.via_recorder_hint: This window reaches the management portal through a recorder: the browser for recording, step-by-step debugging and manual logins opens on this computer; scenarios still run on the server or a worker.
target.local_url_warning_via_recorder: This scenario's URL points to the local computer (127.0.0.1, localhost). workers.form_kind_hint: A worker runs scenarios; a recorder opens the browser for recording, step-by-step debugging and manual logins on that computer (for example your Mac).
recorders.list: RPA Recorder (recording, step-by-step debugging, manual login)
recorders.hint: When you work through a recorder the browser opens on it; scenarios still run on the server or a worker

recorders.empty: No recorders yet. Choose Add device and pick RPA Recorder.
recorders.invite_app: On the computer you record on, open RPA Recorder and paste this invitation (it has been copied to the clipboard); with a development setup you can also use the command below.
recorders.menus_legend: Extra menus shown when the portal is opened through “{name}”
recorders.menus_hint: Hidden by default; this only changes the menus, not permissions

error.recorder_restarted: Recorder {name} restarted, so this session has ended

error.domain_has_composites: Domain {id} still has {count} composite scenario(s); delete or move them first

error.sync_rejected: The remote just got new commits; push again

composite.archived_hint: Archived composite scenarios cannot run; unarchive it on its page
sync.title: Source & sync
sync.description: Keeps the domain folder in sync with a directory in a git repository. Only definitions and validation and publication records are synced, never login states, Secrets or run records.
sync.test_title: Can connect and authenticate; whether the remote branch and directory exist
sync.pull_title: Fetch new remote commits, check them, apply them here and reload
sync.push_title: Commit local changes and push them (never forced)
sync.git_missing: This server has no usable git (2.25 or later): git sync is off; local domains work as usual.
sync.hint_local: No git source; the data lives only on this server.
sync.hint_unchecked: Not connected to the remote yet: Test connection or Pull and reload first.
sync.hint_synced: Local and remote are the same.
sync.hint_ahead: {changes} local changes are not pushed yet.
sync.hint_behind: The remote has {remote} new commits: pull to see them.
sync.hint_diverged: {changes} local changes and {remote} new remote commits: pushing merges them (only a file changed differently on both sides is a conflict).
sync.hint_empty: The remote repository is empty or does not have this branch yet: the first push creates it.
sync.hint_no_directory: The remote does not have this directory yet: the first push creates it and leaves the repository's other directories alone.
sync.hint_conflict: The last sync stopped at a conflict: the same file was changed differently on both sides. Local data stays in use; choose what to do below.
sync.hint_error: The last connection failed; local data is still used.
sync.counts: revisions {revisions}, validation records {verifications}, publications and settings {publications}, other {others}
sync.conflict_body: These files were changed differently here and on the remote. Nothing was applied and the remote was not overwritten.
sync.conflict_hint: After pushing to a new branch, open a PR on GitHub, merge it and pull. Using the remote first backs this domain folder up to backups/. Edit a scenario on one server at a time.
sync.pushed_branch: The local content was pushed to branch {branch}.
sync.source_hint: Each server has its own settings; tokens and private keys stay in this server's data folder
sync.directory_hint: Path in the repository; one repository can hold several domains, one directory each
sync.token_saved: Saved; leave empty to keep it
sync.https_hint: GitHub does not accept passwords for git: use a fine-grained personal access token with read and write access to Contents of this repository only.
sync.ssh_hint: Generate a deploy key, then add the public key to the repository's Deploy keys with write access. SSH does not use a username or password.
sync.paste_key: Or paste your own private key
sync.host_keys: Host fingerprints recorded on first connection:
sync.auto_pull: Pull when the server starts (if the remote cannot be reached, start with the last local data)
sync.public_warning: Anyone can read a public repository. Use a private repository when scenarios contain internal URLs, account names or default values.
sync.nothing_to_push: There are no local changes to push; pushing also fetches new remote commits.
sync.probe_empty: Empty repository: the first push creates branch {branch}.
sync.probe_no_branch: The remote has no branch {branch} yet: the first push creates it.
sync.probe_no_directory: Connected: branch {branch} does not have this directory yet; the first push creates it.
sync.startup_pull_failed: Could not pull domain {id}; using the last local data: {detail}
sync.block_sensitive: {path}: looks like a login state, Secrets or a private key and cannot be pushed
sync.block_suffix: {path}: only yaml, json, py, md and txt files can be pushed
sync.warn_problems: The domain folder has {count} load problems (others will see them after the push)
sync.warn_dependency_local: Composite scenarios depend on domain {domain}, which has no git source: others will be missing the dependency after pulling
sync.warn_dependency_unpushed: Revision {revision} of {scene}, used by a composite scenario, is not on the remote of domain {domain} yet: push {domain} too
sync.branch_message: {domain}: local content pushed after a conflict
replays.description: Runs that still have a recording. Play it, find the moment by its thumbnails and follow the steps; a failed run opens just before the failed step.
replays.summary_on: Recording is on: passed runs keep the video for {passed} days, others for {other} days, at most {limit} GB in total.
replays.summary_off: Recording is off: new runs are not recorded; existing recordings follow the retention rules.
replays.settings_hint: Other results are failed, timed out, cancelled and needs login. 0 days deletes the video when the run ends. Over the limit, the oldest are deleted first; pinned ones are kept. Only videos are deleted: run records, reports and screenshots stay.
replays.empty: No recordings yet. While recording is on, validations and executions are recorded.
replay.title: Replay {id}
replay.previous_failed_title: The previous run of this scenario that did not pass
replay.not_finished: The run has not finished yet; it can be replayed when it ends.
replay.url_hint: The page URL at this moment (the video only shows the page; the URL comes from the step records)
replay.end_failed_hint: The independent assertions and outputs did not run.
replay.cannot_play: This window cannot play the video (WebM). Open the management portal's website in Chrome, Edge or Firefox, or download the video.
replay.key_step: Start of the previous / next step
replay.not_seekable: This video was not finished properly when the run was interrupted and could not be repaired: it plays from the start but cannot be seeked.
replay.repaired: This video was repaired after the run was interrupted; the last few seconds may be missing.
replay.no_checks: This scenario has no assertions, or they did not run.
replay.checks_hint: Assertions and outputs run after the browser closes, so they are not in the video; they do not run when the automation fails.
replay.keep_until: Kept by the retention rules until
replay.no_video_running: The run has not finished yet.
replay.no_video_deleted: The recording was deleted by the retention rules ({reason}); the run record, report and screenshots are still here.
replay.deleted_expired: kept longer than the retention days
replay.no_video_failed: The recording of this run was not saved ({error}).
replay.no_video_script: Python script scenarios are not recorded.
replay.no_video_off: This run has no recording: recording was off, or the run happened before recording was added.
replayjs.located_failed: Jumped to step {{n}}, where the run failed
replayjs.copy_link: Copy a link to this moment
replayjs.copy_failed: Could not copy; select it yourself: {{link}}
replayjs.beyond_video: Video coverage ends at {{time}}. Later steps have no recorded frames; this does not imply an execution failure.
replayjs.no_steps: This run has no step records.
replayjs.pin: Pin so it is not deleted
replayjs.pin_failed: Could not pin; please try again.
spec.dynamic_title: Replaced with the current value each time a run starts (today's date, a random number…)
replay.missing_clip: No recording for this page at this time. Check the step records for execution results.
replayjs.missing_pages: Some page recordings are missing. All steps remain on the timeline; missing intervals are marked.

updates.device_off: Automatic updates are off (the server runs {version})

agent.openapi_description: API for third-party agent systems: write scenes, debug on a recorder, and have workers validate and run them; combine scenes into composite scenes in projects, validate, publish and run them, and follow run progress. Send Authorization: Bearer <API key> with every request. See the Agent guide in the engineering docs.
agents.description: Third-party agent systems use the Agent API to write scenes, debug on recorders, and have workers validate and run them. Each agent system gets one client and one key.
agents.notice: A key is shown only once, when the client is created or the key is regenerated; the server stores only its hash. New clients can only read; publishing (scenes:publish, projects:publish) and page content are off by default, so turn them on only after confirming the agent may receive internal pages. See the Agent guide in the engineering docs.
agents.api_off: The external port is off (rpa serve --worker-port), so agents cannot connect
agents.audit_hint: Every write request from agents (including rejected ones), latest 100; cannot be edited or deleted
agents.form_notice: Restrictions beyond scopes: anything unchecked is not allowed; "All" means no restriction.
agents.form_id_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens; cannot be changed later

agents.scope_scenes_write: Create scenes, save revisions, edit inputs and outputs, import scripts
agents.scope_debug: Open debug sessions on allowed recorders
agents.scope_runs_validate: Have workers validate any revision of a scene or composite scene
agents.scope_runs_execute: Run scenes and composite scenes for real, cancel and rerun
agents.scope_runs_read: Read the status and results of runs and composite runs
agents.scope_projects_read: Read projects, composite scenes, revisions and the scene library
agents.scope_projects_write: Create and edit projects; create and save composite scenes

agents.page_content_hint: If the agent uses an external model, this content leaves your network; turn it on only after confirming that is acceptable.
agents.allowed_ips_hint: IPs or networks separated by commas or spaces; leave empty for no restriction
agents.key_notice: This key is shown only now and cannot be viewed again after you close this dialog; hand it to the agent system's administrator and never put it in logs or scenes.

recorders.agent_hint: The API client must allow this recorder too
js.agent_rotate_body: The old key stops working immediately; the agent system must switch to the new key.
